name: Marlin
tagline: the drifter: the nose is free, the velocity is yours to earn
summary: The drifter. Velocity and nose are two different things: the sticks turn the hull freely while it keeps sliding, RT burns along the nose, LT is a retro burn against the velocity, B flips it 180° in a third of a second (flip and burn). A drift assist bends the velocity gently toward the nose so it reads as 3D drifting rather than a physics puzzle; turn it to 0 in Vessel Config for pure Newtonian flight.

spec.v: RT thrust · LT retro · B flip · velocity decoupled
3D drift: Chorus's Drift Trance; Squadrons; Everspace 2

fantasy: It points one way and goes another. A corner is a slide you set up two seconds early, and a chase is a dance of flips.
why: Arcade flight players want tight, drifting, momentum-preserving ships, not sims (Squadrons 'pure arcade joy', Chorus's Drift Trance 'car drifting in three dimensions and zero gravity, feels incredible', Jett panned for fiddly controls). Every Cosmic Shore hull tracks its throttle; the Marlin is the one whose speed is a vector you carry, with an assist dial so the first session rewards.

charge.name: Main Burn
charge.tip: Charge is the main engine's thrust.

mass.name: Momentum
mass.tip: Mass is how much velocity it can carry.

space.name: Retro
space.tip: Space is the braking burn's strength.

time.name: Agility
time.tip: Time is how fast the free nose turns.

styles.name: Balanced
styles.info: Every element at 0: the recipe's numbers.

styles.name: Racer
styles.info: Big burns and a high cap: fast and committed.

styles.name: Duellist
styles.info: Quick nose and strong retro: stops and turns on a thought.

styles.name: Maxed
styles.info: Every element at 10. A ceiling, not a match state.

notModelled: The game's throttle axis (the sticks' spread) is unused: throttle is RT. This is a second input strategy, like the Dragonfly's.
The assist is one lateral-damping number; a shipped version would want the Dolphin's drift-hold shape and a camera that reads the slip.
sources: Design: Docs/Studios/CONCEPT_FLEET.md (Marlin). Nearest shipped relatives: the Dolphin's locked drift (velocity frozen, no thrust) and the Squirrel's live-thrust drift.
